editor_note: The RBI raised its rate for the first time in more than three years and dropped its neutral stance. The lead says what that does to a home loan.
house_note: Djokovic has now played 34 matches in Beijing and lost none. At 39 he treats the place like a home fixture.

lead.headline: RBI raises the repo rate to 5.5%, its first rise since 2023, and shuts the door on cuts for now
lead.short: All six members of the Monetary Policy Committee voted for the 25 basis point rise, and the stance moved from neutral to "calibrated tightening". The RBI raised its inflation forecast for this year to 5.2% from 5.0%, and its growth forecast to 7.1% from 6.7%. At 13:45 the Sensex was down about 420 points, with car makers among the biggest fallers.
more: On a ₹40 lakh home loan over 25 years at 7.5%, BankBazaar's Adhil Shetty puts the rise at about ₹654 a month once a lender passes it on; many lenders stretch the tenure instead of raising the EMI, which costs more over the life of the loan. Loans linked to the repo rate move first. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the UPI merchant fee that starts on 15 October should not dent volumes.

why.text: Floating-rate loans get dearer at their next reset, deposit rates should follow, and the new stance says this may not be the last rise: Geojit's VK Vijayakumar expects two more.

update.new: The RBI raised the repo rate to 5.5% and changed its stance to tightening.
update.front: The first rate rise in more than three years changes loan and deposit rates for every household; it leads on its own.

seconds.headline: Djokovic wins a seventh Beijing title at 39, the 102nd of his career, when de Minaur retires
seconds.short: He had won a tight first set 7–6 when de Minaur stopped in the second with an apparent groin injury. Djokovic is now 34–0 in Beijing and has won a title in 21 straight seasons; only Jimmy Connors (109) and Roger Federer (103) have won more in the Open Era. He climbs to No. 8 on Monday.

why.text: The first title since Athens last November, won the week Sinner's season ended; Shanghai starts today.

update.front: A title for Novak is front-page news for this reader.

seconds.headline: Shreyas Iyer's 102 not out from 43 balls wins the first T20I by eight wickets
seconds.short: West Indies were all out for 171 in 19.1 overs, and India got there with 32 balls to spare. Iyer, captain and batting at No. 4, hit ten fours and six sixes in his first T20I hundred, and became the first India captain to make one while chasing. India lead the five-match series 1–0; the second game is in Ranchi on Friday.

why.text: A first hundred in the first game as T20 captain settles who leads this young side.

update.new: India won the first T20I; Iyer made 102 not out.
update.front: A captain's hundred on debut as T20 captain is the cricket news of the week.

seconds.headline: Messi scores in his last match for Argentina, a 3–0 win over Benin, and leaves in tears
seconds.short: In front of 85,000 at the Monumental he set up Nicolás Otamendi's opener and scored a 71st-minute penalty, his 126th goal in 208 matches over 21 years; Nico Paz scored the other. The game stopped in the 10th minute for a minute's ovation, and a drone show followed the final whistle. He called it the saddest day of his football life.

why.text: The end of the international career of the man most people call the best ever.

update.new: The farewell match was played: a goal and an assist.
update.front: The last game of Messi's international career is front-page news on its own.

seconds.headline: Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi booked for trespass; the Chief Justice will consider recalling the split verdict on the CEC law
seconds.byline: INDIAN EXPRESS · LIVE LAW · SCROLL · 7 OCT
seconds.short: Delhi Police registered an FIR over Tuesday's seven-hour sit-in inside Akashvani Bhawan, 200 metres from the Election Commission, where the march by about 200 INDIA bloc MPs was stopped. On Wednesday Chief Justice Surya Kant agreed to examine a plea to recall September's split verdict on the 2023 law that took the Chief Justice off the panel choosing election commissioners; the plea says the son of one judge on that bench is the Commission's standing counsel. Gyanesh Kumar has put off a visit to Chhattisgarh.

why.text: The protest has moved from the street to a police case, and the law behind his appointment is back before the court.

update.new: An FIR against the Gandhis, and the Chief Justice agreed to look at recalling the verdict on the appointments law.
update.front: Two new turns on the same day in the dispute over the Election Commission.

briefs.headline: Airtel raises postpaid plans by ₹50 from Thursday, adding one free roaming pack a year
briefs.text: Existing customers move to the nearest higher plan within a month. The yearly pack gives 5GB, 60 minutes of calls and 25 texts for five days abroad, and each member of a family plan gets one.

briefs.text: Both completed Tuesday's full session as the internationals began to return; Madrid play Villarreal at the Bernabéu on Saturday night, 00:30 IST on Sunday.

briefs.text: In a statement of nearly 2,000 words the 41-year-old said he deserves to be punished for leaving the camp after he was left out against Norway and told he would not start against Denmark.

update.new: Ronaldo gave his side of the walk-out.

briefs.text: Anirudh Thapa scored India's goal; the crowd was sparse despite cuts of up to 90% in ticket prices and free passes.

preview.text: Marina Bay is slow, bumpy and hot: braking, traction and rear grip out of tight corners decide it, overtaking is hard, so qualifying and the safety car matter. Mercedes call it a stronghold, but their Sepang upgrade made the car slower in low-speed corners, and Singapore is where they will find out why. Verstappen arrives from his first win of the year, his third straight top-two finish.

briefs.text: His third title of a season broken up by a wrist injury, and his first since Doha; he is only the third man to win Tokyo twice in a row.

briefs.headline: Three new Supreme Court judges sworn in; the court is one short of its full strength of 38
briefs.text: Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh, formerly chief justices of Gujarat, Delhi and Telangana, took the oath; Justice Agarwal makes three women among 37 judges.

briefs.headline: Russia fires about 70 missiles and drones at Kyiv and other regions; at least 11 dead
briefs.text: Zelenskyy said energy was a main target; Moscow said it hit arms factories, including the maker of the Flamingo cruise missile.

briefs.headline: WHO asks Russia for details after a worker at a Siberian plague laboratory dies
briefs.text: Officials are still looking for the cause; they say everyone who was in contact with the researcher tested negative for pneumonic plague.

briefs.headline: OpenAI publishes 722 papers of maths results from an unreleased model
briefs.text: The papers, posted on GitHub, cover 372 groups of results and include some of the model's reasoning and the compute it used; mathematicians will take time to check them.

briefs.headline: ChatGPT text will carry a hidden watermark by default in the EU
briefs.text: The EU AI Act requires it; elsewhere it is optional. OpenAI's own tests show editing a fifth of the text cuts detection by almost 75%.

briefs.headline: Physics Nobel goes to Francis Halzen, who built IceCube to catch neutrinos in Antarctic ice
briefs.text: Thousands of sensors frozen into a cubic kilometre of ice at the South Pole pick up the flashes of rare high-energy neutrinos from distant galaxies.

briefs.headline: Cabinet splits Bengaluru police into five commissionerates under a chief commissioner
briefs.text: The split follows the Greater Bengaluru Authority's five corporations; serving and retired officers are divided on it.

screen.title: Drishyam: The Conclusion
screen.reason: A satisfying close to the franchise: Devgn's silent Vijay and Jaideep Ahlawat's cop carry it, though critics differ on how much the slow first half and the courtroom twists cost it.

screen.title: Verity
screen.reason: Most critics found the Colleen Hoover thriller silly and unconvincing, wasting Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson; a few enjoyed it as knowing camp.

screen.title: Resident Evil
screen.reason: Zach Cregger's reboot is gory, fast and often funny, with Austin Abrams a likeable lead; its critics say the chaos outruns any real dread.

screen.title: Heart of the Beast
screen.reason: An old-fashioned man-and-dog survival story in Alaska, lifted by Brad Pitt and the dog; reviews run from deeply moving to serviceable.

screen.title: The Uprising
screen.reason: Andrew Garfield is committed and the battle scenes hit hard, but most critics found Paul Greengrass's Peasants' Revolt epic thin, grim and flat.

screen.title: Mirzapur: The Movie
screen.reason: Fan service done well: Pankaj Tripathi's Kaleen Bhaiya and the dialogue carry it, though almost every critic says its 197 minutes sag in the second half.
